title: What the carrier kept
intro: The owner wants their property home. The person borrowing it still needs one more shift.
findings: An old mark identifies a keeper from before the loan.
The newest wear records work the owner has never seen.
choices: Return it with a tracing of its wear
Extend the loan and give the owner a dated receipt
effects: The owner holds it again. The next borrower must work from the tracing.
The current crew can finish its work. The owner has only the receipt until collection.

title: Vesper’s unpaid account
intro: A paid invoice and a delivery entry sit in the same column. One of them is being used as a promise.
tools: Lay the delivery against its date
findings: The deposit paid for permission to start.
The signed delivery came later and covered a smaller order.
choices: Post the deposit and receipt together
Hold the receipt at the counter for questions
effects: Anyone can see the mismatch. A buyer asks for an explanation in public.
The clerk can explain what changed. The person who leaves early sees one figure.

title: The apprentice’s second try
intro: An apprentice has copied a master's result. They want the right to put a different test beside it.
findings: The known arrangement gives the promised result on the first try.
The result shifts when one setting changes. The apprentice writes down the setting.
choices: Leave both runs with the apprentice
Invite the master to repeat the surprising run
effects: The apprentice gets credit and the job of showing the next visitor.
The master lends a name to the work. The apprentice waits for the public demonstration.

title: The travelling refrain
intro: Two crews remember the same tune with different rests. The rest is where the next crew comes in.
tools: Beat out the first crew’s entry
findings: The opening voice keeps time until the crossing.
The answering voice leaves a longer rest so a late worker can join.
choices: Keep the two entries in separate parts
Teach one shared entry and name the rest
effects: Both crews can recognise their own part. A new singer needs a guide.
Everyone can start together. The longer quiet survives only in the margin.

title: An atlas with loose corners
intro: One corner of the map curls away. Under it someone has written directions from the other end of the road.
tools: Turn the map toward the returning walker
findings: The outward instructions work until the last turning.
From the other side the landmark disappears behind a roof.
choices: Pin two arrows with their starting places
Leave one arrow and add a guide at the turn
effects: Returning travellers get an arrow too. The board needs twice the space.
A guide can hear exactly where someone started. The turn depends on a person being there.

title: A hand missing from the roll
intro: A witness appears on the duty rota and vanishes from the published roll.
findings: The rota gives a time at which the witness could have been there.
The carbon records a change of hand before anyone signed.
choices: Hold a space for the missing name
Sign the claim narrowly and leave a return address
effects: The blank stays visible. The family has to see it at every visit.
An interested reader can write back. A hurried reader sees a finished line.

title: Footsteps beside the satchel
intro: A small creature waits beside the satchel. It moves whenever somebody moves the lamp.
findings: With the lamp shaded the creature comes closer to the warmth.
An empty satchel draws it only when the familiar keeper is there.
choices: Leave a quiet perch and take the light
Invite the keeper to travel with it
effects: The creature chooses its own distance. The watcher has to come back.
Two familiar footsteps travel together. The keeper gives up their usual round.

title: The letter with two addresses
intro: Two people want the same letter. One was promised an answer and the other was promised privacy.
tools: Hold the envelope to the routing light
Read the permission on the outer flap
findings: The second postmark belongs to a forwarding desk.
The writer permitted one line to be read aloud, with the rest under the flap.
choices: Read the permitted line and carry the rest
Bring the two recipients to the same desk
effects: The first reader gets an answer today. The carrier has another journey.
Both can check the permission together. The reply waits for the later arrival.

title: The fair after dark
intro: A fair opens while half its crew are still at work. The first visitors will set the story everyone else hears.
tools: Try the opening from the queue
Walk the stall after the first bell
findings: The first visitors can see the demonstration and ask the maker.
Late arrivals get the result without the demonstration.
choices: Keep a repeat show for the late crew
Send a working model with the first visitors
effects: The late crew can ask in person. The maker takes the evening shift.
The model reaches people early. Their neighbours have to explain what the maker saw.

title: The favour written in pencil
intro: A trusted visitor can enter first. Someone at the back wants the same chance to check a decision.
findings: The key opens a view that the public desk has left out.
The public channel leaves a trace, but its reply will take another shift.
choices: Lend the key in the presence of a witness
Keep the return channel staffed through supper
effects: A stranger sees the original. Their visit costs the keeper one private hour.
Nobody needs special access. The evening keeper misses supper with a friend.

title: A companion’s unfinished shift
intro: A companion promises to finish somebody else’s shift. That promise has already been counted twice.
tools: Move one worker to the relief bench
findings: The old rota has one name beside two simultaneous jobs.
A relief worker can take one job if someone teaches the hand signal.
choices: Teach the signal and share the shift
Cover the shift now and bring the rota back
effects: A new person can take the job tomorrow. Tonight's handover takes longer.
Tonight's promise holds. The next crew inherits a correction to make.

title: A Fray in the lamplight
intro: A Fray grows whenever a narrow finding is repeated as a promise to everyone.
tools: Turn the claim back to its source
Try it with a different audience
findings: Under its original conditions the narrow claim holds.
A new listener hears a guarantee the first speaker never gave.
choices: Keep the claim with its conditions
Leave both listeners’ readings on the lamp
effects: The Fray folds into a small, readable shadow. The sign takes longer to read.
The shadow splits so each listener can see the other. The disagreement remains visible.
